Ψ ψ.definition: indecl., twenty-third letter of the Ionic alphabet, Pl.Cra.427a, Callias ap.Ath.10.453d: not used in the Attic alphabet: in the Western Gr. alphabets it represents the sound : with the value ps it is found in SIG1 , e…

ψάγδαν.definition: or an Egyptian unguent; the following forms are found: Eub.102; Ar.Fr.206; Eup.198; Epil.1: is cited by Erot. fr. Hp. , and fr. Eup.: nom. Ath.15.690e, cf. Hsch

ψάγιος.definition: oblique, askew, metaph., mal à propos, blundering, Pi.N.7.69: Hsch.; Id

ψαθυρότης.definition: looseness of consistency, Arist.HA524b26, Pr.928a10, Gal.6.799

ψαινύθιος.definition: false, vain, Hsch.:—Lyc.1420 has prophesy falsely

ψακάδιον.definition: later Dim. of drizzle, Polioch.2.5, Thphr.CP2.9.3

ψάκαλον.definition: new-born animal, Ar.Byz. ap. Eust.1625.48; Id. ap. Ael.NA7.47: in cod. Hsch

ψακαλοῦχος.definition: having young, mothers with their young, S.Fr.793 ; cf

ψάκιον.definition: Dim. of small piece or drop, Hsch

ψαλάκανθα.definition: name of a fabulous plant, Eub.28 , Ptol.Heph. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.150B

ψαλάκιος.definition: perh. an occupational name, dub. in PLond.3.604.40

ψαλίδιον.definition: pair of scissors, POxy.1289.5,6 (v; as pr. name, Scissors, nickname of Alexander Logotheta, because he clipped the coins, Procop.Arc.26, Goth.3.1

ψαλληγενής.definition: sprung from harp-playing, Com. epith. of Archytas, strictly a parody of Homer's Bion ap. D.L.4.52

ψαλμοχαρής.definition: delighting in harp-playing, of Apollo, AP9.525.24

ψάμμη.definition: rarer form of Hdt.4.181 , who elsewh. always has the common form: Dor. A.Pr.573 , Ar.Lys.1261

ψάμμητον.definition: a kind of cake, Harp. s.v

ψάμμος.definition: but in Archim.Aren.1.1, al., always; metallic ore used by alchemists, in pl., Olymp.Alch.p.106B., Zos.Alch.p.239 B

ψάρ.definition: gen. pl. Ion. Sturnus vulgaris, . . Il.17.755; 16.583; dat. Q.S.8.387, 11.218; Antiph.302 , AP9.373, Gal.6.567; Plu.2.972f mentions their being taught to speak, cf. Gell.13.21 .25

ψαρομαχία.definition: battle of the starlings, Suid. s.v

ψαρός.definition: like a starling, i. e. speckled, dappled, a dapple-grey horse, Ar.Nu.1225, LXXZa.1.8; Arist.HA632b19 distinguishes it fr. which implies that the spots are more distinctly marked:—Comp. Ael.NA12.28, Aët.11.11

ψαυκροπόδης.definition: and , swift- footed, epith. of the horse Arion, EM817.45, Hsch

ψαῦσις.definition: touching, contact, Democr.11, Plu.2.683c, Sor.Fract.13, Gal.18.786:—esp. of lovers, caress, Plu.Alc.4, cf. 2.768b

ψαφαρόθριξ.definition: with dry, rough hair or coat, h.Pan.32

ψεῖ.definition: name of the letter Hellad. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.530 B

ψελλότης.definition: imperfect pronunciation, distd. fr. by Arist.Pr.902b24; Plu.2.963c

ψεμμή.definition: a weight, = 1/3 of a II.5, HeroGeom.23.61

ψευδάριον.definition: fallacy, in pl. title of work by Euclid, Procl.in Euc.p.70F., cf. p.59 F

ψευδαριστοφάνειος.definition: a pretended follower of Aristophanes, Ath.1.5b

ψευδηρακλῆς.definition: sham-Hercules, name of a Comedy by Menander, Plu.2.59c, Ath.4.172a

ψευδισόδομος.definition: built of equal blocks, but in courses of unequal size, Vitr.2.8.5

ψευδόμαντις.definition: false prophet, Hdt.4.69, A.Ag.1195, S.OC1097, E.Or.1667, etc

ψευδομάρτυς.definition: false witness, pl. in Gorg.Pal.23, Pl.Grg.472b, Critias61: sg., IG5.357.4 : false witnesses about God, 1 Ep.Cor.15.15; as Adj., the action for false witness, IG l.c. 1.8; honours attesting no real merit, Plu.2.821f

ψευδορρήμων.definition: gen. false locutions, perh. made-up words, Phld.Po.2.41

ψεῦδος.definition: Ep. dat. pl. v. I.2; in Logic, false conclusion, fallacy, Arist.APr.61b3; ib.37a36:—in NT of what is opposed to religious truth, false doctrine, Ep.Rom.1.25; i.e. doing what is repugnant to the true faith, Apoc.21.27;…

ψευδοστιγματίας.definition: a false or pretended name of a play by Nicostr.Com

ψευδουργός.definition: one who practices deceitful arts, Pl.Sph.241b

ψευδόχρυσος.definition: a false chrysolite, D.S.2.52; of mock gold, Plu.2.50a

ψευσίστυξ.definition: hating falsehood, epith of Apollo, AP9.525.24

ψέφος.definition: darkness, cj. Lobeck in Alc.112 , cf. Gal.19.156; = Hsch

ψήν.definition: gen. gall-insect, Cynips psenes, which; fruit of the made palm, Poll.1.244

ψῆξις.definition: rubbing down, currying, of horses, X.Eq.5.3,10

ψῆττα.definition: a kind of flat-fish, prob. turbot, Rhombus; a nickname for a glutton, Pl.Com.106. Suid.)

ψῆφος.definition: Dor. Aeol. gen. pl; precious stone, gem, Philostr.VA3.27; esp. worn in a ring, Luc.DMeretr.9

ψιά.definition: = Hsch: hence Dor. play, sport, Ar.Lys.1302 ; Hsch

ψιαθοπλόκος.definition: a plaiter of mats, PSI10.1132.8 , Greg. Cor.p.551S., Lex.Herodot.ap.SteinHerodotusii p.458, Suid. s.v. written in Sammelb.5124.332 :—also Gloss

ψιάς.definition: = drop, Il.16.459, cf. Hes.Sc.384: also , Hsch.; cf

ψίδιον.definition: pl. prob. engraver's error for IG11.161 B 19, 287 B 21 : v

ψίθιος.definition: Adj., name of a kind of grape, Dsc.5.5, cf. Verg.G.2.93, 4.269, Stat.Silv.4.9.38; Nic.Al.181: hence was made Eub.138 , cf. Anaxandrid.71, Plin.HN14.80:—also spelt Docum. ined. dell' Africa Italiana1.86, al. , v.l. in …

ψίθυρ.definition: = a form actually found acc. to EM506.31, cf. Sch.Theoc.1.1

ψιθύρα.definition: a Libyan odyte) musical instrument, identified by some with the Poll.4.60; S.Inach. in PTeb.692 iii 1

ψίλαξ.definition: epith. of Dionysus at Amyclae, Paus.3.19.6; he explains it as winged , which suggests that it has

ψίλιον.definition: = armlet, IG11.161 B 26, 162 B 15, 199 B 57, 203 B82 , Inscr.Délos296B37 ; : . . Hsch.; also IG11.203A4 : v

ψιττακός.definition: parrot, Call.Iamb.1.167, PMag.Par.2.508; an eye-salve, Gal.12.745.—On the accent, v. Hdn.Gr.1.150

ψόα.definition: or more freq. in pl. or muscles of the loins , Hp.Art.45 , Nat.Hom.11 , cf. Oss.18 , Morb.Sacr.3 , and LXXLe.3.9, 2 Ki.2.23, Ps.37.8, al.; Euphro7, Clearch.72, Aret.CD2.3 ; acc. pl. Polybus ap.Arist.HA512b21: LXXLe. l…

ψόθος.definition: = Phryn.Com.95 , Phot., Suid.); = acc. to Theognost.Can.54

ψοΐτης.definition: lumbar portion of the spinal cord, Gal.8.328

ψόρος.definition: an unknown fish, Numen. ap. Ath.7.313e; also Speus. ibid

ψύγμα.definition: a means of cooling, anything that; a cooling lotion, Hp.Morb.2.16 ; a cooling medicine, Id.Aff.11

ψυγμός.definition: chilliness, dampness, Porph.Abst.1.28; cold fit of an ague, or rigor caused by poison, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.17, Dsc.5.11, Gal.11.519, Poll.4.186; cf

ψυδρεύς.definition: name of a month at Corcyra, IG9.682

ψύθος.definition: poet. collat. form for lie, untruth, A.Ag.478 , 999 , 1089 :—in Call.Fr.184, is a Subst. in appos. with

ψύλλα.definition: a venomous spider, perhaps Lathrodectes or malmignatte, Arist.HA622b31

ψύλλιον.definition: or flea-wort, Plantago Psyllium, Dsc.4.69, Luc.Trag.157

ψυλλοτοξότης.definition: flea-archer, flea-skirmisher, Comic word in Luc.VH1.13

ψῦξις.definition: a cooling, chilling; a being or becoming cold, ib.16; Pl.Ti.85d: pl., opp. Id.Tht.156b; opp. Lg.897a, Arist.GA777b27

ψῦχος.definition: cold, Emp.65.2; opp; once in Hom., coolness, Od.10.555: metaph., A.Ag.971

ψυχοφθόρος.definition: destructive of life, deadly; soul-destroying, Ph.Fr.103 H., cf. Cod.Just.1.1.5.3

ψώα.definition: rottenness, putrid stench, A.R.Fr.5: but Hdn.Epim.155

ψωθίον.definition: small crumb, morsel, Pherecr.81 :—also blister on under- surface of loaf, Poll.7.23; hence of coin used in Hades, Pherecr. l. c

ψωλή.definition: Dor. prop. fem. of membrum virile praeputio retracto, Ar.Lys.143, Av.560 , Supp.Epigr.3.596

ψωλός.definition: with the prepuce drawn back, Ar.Av.507 , Eq.964, Pl.267, Diph.39

ψώμηξ.definition: a grub that eats the roots of corn, Hsch

ψωμός.definition: morsel, bit, gobbets of man's flesh, Od.9.374, cf. Amips.19.2 , X.Mem.3.14.5, Pericles ap. Arist.Rh.1407a2, Plb.30.26.6; LXXJd.19.5, al

ψαθάλλω.definition: scratch, rub, scratch my head, Hermipp.78, cf. Pl.Com.59

ψαίρω.definition: only pres., and not in Att. Prose; trans., graze, brush lightly, touch gently, . . is ready to skim the path of ether, A.Pr.396; rub, scrape gently in washing, Eun.VSp.486B

ψαίω.definition: = , rub away, grind down, in aor. 1 Med., Thphr. ap.Porph.Abst.2.6:—aor. Pass., ibid

ψακάδισσα.definition: spotted, dappled, of a mare, prob. in PPetr. 2p.115

ψακάζω.definition: later :—rain in small drops, drizzle, drip, Ar.Nu.580: impers., it drizzles, let it rain loaves, Nicoph.13:—Med., . . they like n a short-sighted person to a spluttering lamp, prob. in Arist.Rh.1413a4 :—Pass., moisten…

ψαλάσσω.definition: later Att. like touch lightly, Ael.NA3.18; make a string sound by touching it, Lyc.139:—aor. 1 Med. in Hsch

ψαλιδοειδής.definition: like a vault or arch, Ph.Bel.81.35, Gal.UP8.11

ψαλιδόστομος.definition: nipper-mouthed, Com. epith. of crabs, Batr.295

ψαλίζω.definition: fut. Anacreont.9.4: :—clip with scissors, l. c., Archig. ap. Orib.8.2.10, Antyll. ap. eund.7.21.6; Babr.51.4, cf. Aesop.382b: Hsch

ψάλιον.definition: part of the bridle, curb-chain; generally, chain, bond, A.Pr.54 : metaph., Id.Ch.962

ψαλίς.definition: a pair of scissors, among the; razor, expld. by , Poll.2.32, 10.140

ψάλλω.definition: fut. LXXJd.5.3, 1 Ep.Cor.14.15: aor; mostly of the strings of musical instruments, play a stringed instrument with the fingers, and not with the plectron, Pl. l. c., et ibi Sch.; Arist.Pr.919b15; Ath.4.183d; opp. Hdt.…

ψάλμα.definition: tune played on a stringed instrument, AP11.34 , Max.Tyr.37.4

ψαλμός.definition: twitching or twanging with the fingers; mostly of musical strings, Telest.5, cf. Diog.Trag.1.9, Aret.CA1.1

ψαλτήριον.definition: stringed instrument, psaltery, harp, Arist.Pr.919b12, cf. Hippias in PHib.1.13.31, Apollod. ap. Ath.14.636f, Thphr.HP5.7.6, LXXGe.4.21, al., Jul.Or.2.49c

ψάλτης.definition: harper, Men.495, Hippias in PHib.1.13.7, 25, Macho ap.Ath.8.348f, LXX1 Es.5.42, Plu.2.67f, 223f, cf. SIG578.15 ; epith. of Apollo, AP9.525.24. [Oxyt. in Att., parox. in Hellenistic Gr., Choerob.in Theod.1.187H.]

ψάλτρια.definition: female harper, Pl.Prt.347d, Ion Trag.22, Arist.Ath.50.2, Men.319.4, Plu.Caes.10, al

ψαλτῳδέω.definition: sing to the harp, LXX2 Ch.5.13

ψαμαθίς.definition: a sea-fish, elsewh. Numen. ap. Ath.7.327a

ψαμμιαῖος.definition: of the size of a grain of sand, Olymp.in Phd.p.31 N

ψαμμίον.definition: Dim., grain of sand: in pl., of gravel in urine, Ruf.Ren.Ves.3.6, 11, Aret.SD2.3, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.110

ψαμμίτης.definition: from sand, AP9.551; name of a treatise by Archimedes

ψαμμοδύτης.definition: like sand-diver; name for a mole, Cyran.78

ψαμμουργία.definition: and art of extracting gold from sand, Zos.Alch.p.241 B

ψαύω.definition: touch lightly. a way of feeling the pulse, opp. Gal.8.808: metaph., touch upon a subject, notice it slightly, Plb.1.13.8:—Med., c. acc. rei, touch lightly upon a subject, Gal.18.331

ψαφαροχαίτης.definition: gloss on PSI8.892 , restd. fr. Hsch. s.v

ψαφαρόχροος.definition: contr. rough on the surface, squalid, E.Rh.716

ψάω.definition: but always contracted], S.Tr.678, inf; intr., crumble away, vanish, disappear, S.Tr.678

ψέγω.definition: S.OT338, etc.: fut. Pl.Grg.518d: aor. Thgn.611, S.Aj.1130, Pl.Lg.634c, etc.:—Pass., pf. Hp.Acut.51:—blame, censure, Thgn. l.c., A.Ag.186 , 1403; S.OC977, etc.; . . Pl.Tht.177b; Id.Prt.346c; X.HG6.5.49: c. acc. rei, . …

ψείω.definition: = acc. to Hdn.Gr. ap. OrionLex.col.168: but is thus glossed in An.Ox.1.401

ψελιόω.definition: twine, wreathe, AP7.234; Med., put on an armlet, subject of statue by Praxiteles, Plin.HN34.70

ψελλίζω.definition: falter in speech, speak; metaph., of a boy soldier, Philostr.Her.19.2

ψέλλισμα.definition: inarticulate speech, of a child's attempts at talking, Him.Or.23.21; of a nurse's 'baby-talk', Sor.1.109

ψελλισμός.definition: metaph., indistinctness, ib.1066d, unpronounced gout, Plu.Sull.26

ψελλιστής.definition: stammerer, Gloss; of horses who injure their hoofs in the stable, Hippiatr.10

ψευδαγγελέω.definition: to be a false messenger , Ph.1.273; cf. sq

ψευδάγγελος.definition: bringing a false report, lying messenger, Il.15.159; title of play, Arist.Po.1455a14

ψευδάδελφος.definition: false brother, pretended Christian, 2 Ep.Cor.11.26, Ep.Gal.2.4, Gloss

ψευδαλέξανδρος.definition: sham-Alexander, an impostor pretending to the name, J.AJ17.12.2, Luc.Ind.20

ψευδάνωρ.definition: sham man, epith. of Dionysus, Polyaen.4.1

ψευδάργυρος.definition: false silver, i. e. perh.zinc, Str.13.1.56

ψευδατράφαξυς.definition: false orach, Com. name of a plant in Ar.Eq.630; cf

ψευδεγγραφῆς γραφή.definition: an action brought by a citizen to show that he has been wrongly entered in a list of debtors, an action for false entry, Arist.Ath.59.3, cf. Lycurg.Fr.12; IG11.146B29 , cf. Inscr.Délos399A98

ψευδέγγραφος.definition: falsely entered, bogus, Senatus consultum Cic.Att.15.26.1

ψευδενεχυρασία.definition: false seizure of security, prob. in PHal.1.241

ψευδεπίγραφος.definition: with false superscription or title, not genuine, D.H.Dem.57, Inscr.Prien.37.123 ; Plu.2.479e; superficial, Plb.23.5.5

ψευδηγορέω.definition: speak falsely, A.Pr.1032, E.Fr.396, Philem.102.5; . . Opp.C.4.319; . . PMag. Leid.V.10.8

ψευδηλογέω.definition: = dub. in = gloss on Lex. in An.Bachm.1.419, v.l. in Suid. s.v

ψευδοβούνιον.definition: Cretan pimpinell, Pimpinella cretica, Dsc.4.124, Plin.HN24.153

ψευδογαυρόομαι.definition: to be elated on unreal grounds, Tz.H.4.720

ψευδογραφέω.definition: Geom., give a fallacious proof; write false accounts or statements, PEnteux.63.18 , Plb.12.7.6, 16.14.8, PTeb.78.17

ψευδογράφημα.definition: false diagram, fallacious proof, Arist.SE171b12 , Alex.Aphr.in Top.22.20, in SE76.23

ψευδογραφία.definition: = foreg., in pl., Ps.-Archyt. ap; false account, Ath.5.216b

ψευδογράφος.definition: a drawer of false diagrams; writer of falsehoods, Thom.Mag.p.224 R.: = falsarius, Gloss

ψευδοδίκταμνον.definition: false dittany, Ballota acetabulosa, Hp.Nat.Mul.32, Thphr.HP9.16.2, Dsc.3.32

ψευδοδίπτερος.definition: false dipteral, of a temple in which there is only one row of columns along the sides, though there is space left for two, Vitr.3.2.1

ψευδοδοξέω.definition: entertain a false opinion or notion, Epicur.Fr.253, Plb.10.2.3, 16.12.11, Phld.Ir.p.76 W., Ph.1.363, J.AJ9.4.3

ψευδοδοξία.definition: false opinion or notion, Polystr.p.14 W., Phld.D.1.14 , Str.14.5.28, Plu.2.716b, Hierocl.in CA12p.446M., etc

ψευδόδοξος.definition: holding a false opinion or notion, labouring under a delusion, Gal.19.484

ψευδοκατήγορος.definition: false accuser, slanderer, Hsch. s.v. Cat.Cod.Astr.7.112

ψευδοκλητεία.definition: the offence of falsely subscribing one's name as witness to a summons , a prosecution for such false subscription, D.53.17, Arist.Ath.59.3; D.53.15; And.1.74.—This is the form found in Arist. l.c. , in the best codd. …

ψευδοκλητήρ.definition: one who falsely subscribes his name as witness to a summons, Theopomp.Hist.267

ψευδολῃστής.definition: sham robber, name of a Comedy by Timocles

ψευδόλιτρος.definition: Att. for lye or soap made from adulterated soda, Ar.Ra.711

ψευδολογέω.definition: speak falsely, spread false reports, Isoc.10.8, Aeschin.2.119, etc.; give a wrong account, Phld.Sign.21

ψευδολογία.definition: falsehood, Isoc.12.1, D.35.32, etc.: pl., Isoc.12.78, Thphr.Char.8.15

ψευδολογιστής.definition: = sq., name of a treatise by Lucian

ψευδολόγος.definition: speaking falsely, lying, Ar.Ra.1521 ; Plb.31.22.9, cf. Phld.Po.5.14, Gal.Anim.Pass.2.2, etc.; AP9.80

ψευδομαρτυρέω.definition: to be a false witness, bear false witness, Critias61, Pl.R.575b, X.Mem.4.4.11, Arist.Rh.1375a12; LXXEx.20.16, Ev.Marc.14.56

ψευδομαρτυρία.definition: false witness, D.41.16 codd.; Is.12.6 codd.: D.57.53 codd.: but mostly in gen. pl., Pl.Lg.937b; Is.3.6; Arist.Pol.1263b21; to convict, and to be convicted, of perjury, Is.5.15, And.1.7, Lys.10.25, Aeschin.1.85; And.1.…

ψευδοπαρήχησις.definition: use of words of similar sound but different meanings, Eust.29.40

ψευδοπάρθενος.definition: pretended maid or virgin, Hdt.4.180; as Adj., Ach.Tat.8.3

ψευδοπερίπτερος.definition: with false peristyle, of a temple in which the columns on the sides are attached to the walls instead of standing free, Vitr.4.8.6

ψευδόπιθος.definition: false i.e. of a different capacity from the official BCH50.214

ψευδοπλάνης.definition: and prob. lying vagrant, Eust.1762.2, 1742.23, of Odysseus

ψευδοποιέω.definition: give the lie to, expose as false, Id.12.25.4, cf. 12.25c.3, S.E.M.24; folld. by acc. et inf., stigmatize as false the doctrine that . . , Phld.Rh.2.87S

ψευδοπροφήτης.definition: false, lying prophet, J.AJ9.6.6, al., 2 Ep.Pet.2.1, Ph.2.343, etc

ψευδόπτωμα.definition: a technical term of wrestlers, sham or unfair fall from which one starts up again and renews the contest, Plu.Comp.Pel.Marc.1, Sch.Ar.Eq.568, Macar.8.88

ψευδοραψῳδός.definition: false rhapsodist, Hsch., as gloss on

ψευδορκέω.definition: swear falsely, Ar.Ec.603 ; distd. fr. by Chrysipp.Stoic.2.63

ψευδοσέληνον.definition: false moonlight, absence of the moon, Hsch., Suid

ψευδοσοφία.definition: false wisdom, and falsely wise, Philostr.VA8.7

ψευδοσοφιστής.definition: sham-sophist, name of a treatise by Lucian

ψευδόστομα.definition: the false or blind mouth of a river, Str.17.1.18

ψευδόστομος.definition: having false or blind mouths, name of a river in India, Ptol.Geog.7.1.8, al.; = ib.4.5.5, 3.10.2, al.: hence as pr. n., D.S.20.75

ψευδοσυγγραφεύς.definition: a false writer, Tz. in An.Ox.3.332, and write falsely, Id.H.8.185

ψευδόσφηξ.definition: false wasp, a solitary kind, Plin.HN30.98

ψευδοτεχνία.definition: false, spurious art, Sch. Aphthon.in Rh.2.623 W., Serv.Dan.ad Verg.Aen.1.464

ψευδοφαής.definition: shining with false, i.e. borrowed, light, of the moon, D.L.2.1

ψευδυποβολιμαῖος.definition: falsely held to be supposititious; name of plays by Crobylus and Cratin.Jun

ψεύδω.definition: S.Ant.389, etc.: fut. Id.OC628; c. gen., cheat, balk, disappoint one of a thing, E.Hec.1031; A.Pers.472; Ar.Th.870; . . . . X.Cyr.1.5.13; E.Fr.650:—Pass., to be cheated balked, disappointed, of a thing, Hdt.1.141, 5.4…

ψευδώνυμος.definition: under a false name, falsely called, A.Pr.717; Id.Th.670; IG3.1308; Ph.2.161, cf. 2.599; 1 Ep.Ti.6.21; Plu.2.479e; opp. Dam.Pr.399. Adv. by a false name, A.Pr.85, cf. Them.Or.2.30a

ψεῦσμα.definition: lie, untruth, fraud; Sch.Theoc.12.24, cf. Kaibel CGFp.218

ψεύστης.definition: liar, cheat, Il.24.261; Adj., = lying, false, Pi.N.5.29; of a cenotaph, AP7.273 ; . . ib.275 , alluding to Epimenid.1, which is cited by Call.Jov.8, Ep.Tit.1.12

ψῆγμα.definition: that which is rubbed or scraped off, shavings, scrapings, chips, gold-dust, Hdt.4.195; so without Id.1.93, 3.94 sq.; Eub.20; Inscr.Délos 442B89 ; of dust and ashes, A.Ag.442 ; of wood, Philostr.Im.1.11; = Dsc.5.77; Id…

ψηγμάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., Inscr.Délos1429B ii 17 , Placit.1.13.2

ψήκτρα.definition: curry-comb for horses, S.Fr.475, E.Hipp.1174, Ar.Fr.62, AP6.233 , 246 , PSI 4.430.5 , etc. In Hsch. also and and

ψηλαφάω.definition: mostly used in pres.: fut. LXXZa.9.13; c. acc. rei, feel about for, grope or search after, Ar.Pax691; . . Act.Ap.17.27

ψηλάφησις.definition: feeling, touching, palpation, Hp.Steril.213, al., Epicur.Fr.21 , LXXWi.15.15, Plu.Aem.14; tickling, Plu.2.125c, cf. 547b

ψηλαφητής.definition: one who feels, a searcher, Sch.Opp.H.2.435

ψηλαφία.definition: Ion. = touching, Hp.Decent.8, Phld.D.1.13, Aret.CA1.1, Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.2.30; handling, Ph.Bel.56.33

ψηνίζω.definition: to Psenize, alluding to the a Comedy by Magnes so called, Ar.Eq.523

ψηφίζω.definition: fut. Att. Aeschin.2.84: aor; i.e. if you add up the numerical values of the letters in the word Theol.Ar.64

ψήφινος.definition: perh. made of marble, as expl. of AB374: Hsch. : from a marble Harpocrates, PMag.Par.1.1074

ψηφίον.definition: Dim. of small pebble, gravel, Aq.Am.9.9; pellet, Orib.Fr.35

ψηφίς.definition: pebble for reckoning, AP11.365; tessellated work, Chor.p.86B

ψήφισις.definition: voting, only in Locr. acc. sg. IG9 .334.45

ψήφισμα.definition: Dor. Inscr.Cret.1. v; generally, decree, law, Emp.115, cf. Ar.V.378 , Lex ap.And.1.96, LXXEs.3.7, al

ψηφισματοπώλης.definition: one who drives a traffic in Ar.Av.1037; also Arg.Ar.Av

ψηφισμός.definition: the use of pebbles , as gloss on Sch.Th.8.69

ψηφοθεσμία.definition: laying of a mosaic pavement, Inscr. gr. et lat. de la Syrie1.168

ψηφοθέτης.definition: maker of tessellated pavements, Gloss.; written in Epigr.Gr.532 :—hence make such work, JRS 18.171 , Gloss.; and the work itself, ib

ψηφοθήκη.definition: box for counters or ballots, Sch.Ar.Th.1040

ψηφολογέω.definition: = LXXTo.13.17 :—hence HeroStereom.2.35, Lyd.Mag.3.65 , Expl.Arch. de Délos11.261

ψηφοπαικτέω.definition: play juggling tricks, Artem.3.55; juggle away right, Lys.Fr.17

ψηφοπαίκτης.definition: one who juggles with pebbles, Eudox.Com.1, S.E.P.2.250

ψηφοπεριβομβήτρια.definition: jar of pebbles used as a rattle , dub. sens. in Eub.56

ψηφοφορέω.definition: give one's vote, vote, D.H.4.20; elect by vote, D.H.10.56:—Pass., Id.9.43:—sts. written v.l. in Id.4.20

ψηφοφορία.definition: Dor. vote by ballot; judgment, decree, J.AJ4.2.4

ψηφόω.definition: adorn with gems, Lyd.Mag.1.4, cf; work in mosaic, Supp.Epigr.7.993 ; adorn with mosaics

ψήχω.definition: Ar.Fr.42, etc.: fut. X.Eq.4.4:—Pass., aor; scratch, dub. in Jul.Caes.310a

ψιάθιον.definition: Dim. of Philem.26, interpol. in Dsc.5.88: perh. rush-basket, POxy.1923.7 : PBaden29.7

ψίζω.definition: or from the former we have fut. Hsch., pf. Pass. : from the latter, aor. fut. Med. v. infr., cf. on pap, = , or = ; Euph.92:—Med., chew, Lyc.639:—Pass., to be fed, AP9.302

ψιθυρίζω.definition: whisper what one dares not speak out, whisper slanders, Alciphr.3.58, LXXPs.40.7; Them.Or.21.262c:—Pass., Plu.Alc.23

ψιθύρισμα.definition: any low whispering noise, as of trees rustling, Theoc.1.1

ψιθυρισμός.definition: whispering, Phld.Ir.p.55 W; slandering, ib.143f, 2 Ep.Cor.12.20

ψιθυριστής.definition: whisperer, at Athens as epith. of; slanderer, Ep.Rom.1.30

ψίθυρος.definition: whispering, slanderous, S.Aj.148; twittering, of birds, AP12.136; so of music, Ar.Fr.671

ψιλίζομαι.definition: later form for D.C.63.9, al.; cf. Lex.Rhet.ap.Eust.907.38

ψιλογραφέω.definition: write with a single vowel, not a diphthong, Tz.H.5.696

ψιλοκέραμος.definition: or perh. glazed tiles, Inscr.Délos 366 A33, cf. 462 A19 , but = suggrunda , Gloss

ψιλοκιθαριστής.definition: = ), one who plays the without singing to it, instrumental performer, Chares4J., cf. Ath.10.452f, Suet.Dom.4; also CIG2759 :—and = Philoch. l. c.:—cf. IV.3

ψιλόκουρος.definition: smooth-shaved, gloss on , Sch.Call. l. c. , condemned by Phryn.41, who recommends

ψιλομετρία.definition: verse not accompanied by music; prose composition, Them.Or.26.319a

ψιλοποιέω.definition: write with a smooth breathing, Theodoretus in cod. Barocc. 68

ψιλόταπις.definition: a smooth carpet, a carpet without pile, PCair. Zen.48.2 ; opp. Lycon ap.D.L.5.72, cf. Cephisodor. ap. Ath.12.548e, Clearch.25; written in Paus.Gr.Fr.304; cf. II.1

ψιλότης.definition: bareness, Hp.Aër.19, cf; baldness, Id.Galb.27: pl., Artem.1.21

ψιλόφυτος.definition: bare of plants, in the open country, PAvrom.2A6, 2 B 7

ψιλόω.definition: strip bare, mostly of hair; c. gen., strip bare of, Hp.Art.1:—Pass., Id.Aph.5.22, cf. Art.69, Arist.HA519b5

ψίλωθρον.definition: depilatory, Thphr.HP9.20.3, Menemach. ap.Orib.10.14.1, Crito ap.Gal.12.447; used of the plant Nic.Th.902, Dsc.4.182 ; also Hp.Fist.9

ψίλωμα.definition: bone laid bare of flesh, Hp.Art.69, cf. Epid.3.4

ψίλωσις.definition: stripping bare of flesh; Gramm., writing or pronouncing with the spiritus lenis, or an unaspirated consonant, Eust.515.37

ψιλωτής.definition: one who writes or pronounces with the spiritus lenis, or litterae tenues, Tz.H.11.52

ψιμύθιον.definition: = white lead, used as a pigment, esp. to whiten the skin of the face, Ar.Ec.878,929, Amips.3, Dialex.2.6, etc.; even for the hair, Pl.Ly.217d; X.Oec.10.2; . . , Eub.98, cf. Ar.Ec.1072; Jul.Or.7.233b; also used in salv…

ψιμυθιόω.definition: paint with white lead, Plu.Alc.39:—Pass., Lys.1.14, cf. 17, Ath.12.528f: Achaean abs. in Pass., Schwyzer 429 : pf. Pass. Phot

ψιμυθιστής.definition: one who paints with white lead or cosmetics, Gloss

ψίμυθος.definition: radic. form of IG11.145.9 : scanned in AP11.374 , 408

ψίνω.definition: Cretan for IG12.867; part. Philol.50.578:—Med. shed the fruit before ripening, of the vine, Thphr.HP4.14.6: cf. Hsch.: v

ψιχάρπαξ.definition: Crumb-filcher, name of a mouse in Batr.105

ψιχίον.definition: Dim. of crumb, Ev. Matt.15.27; of stomachic residue after emesis, Archig. ap. Orib.8.23.5

ψογέω.definition: or = aor. , LXX1 Ma.11.5, 11: fut. Pass. Vett.Val.119.25; Id.120.37

ψολοκομπία.definition: thunderous talk, i. e. empty noise, Ar.Eq.696

ψοφέω.definition: pf. Men.Sam.324, etc.:—sound, make a; esp. of an empty noise, S.Fr.61; Alex.25.9; Call.Aet.Oxy.2079.19

ψόφημα.definition: noise: pl., bombast, S.Inach. in PTeb.692 ii 7

ψόφησις.definition: making a noise, sounding, Cratin.323 , cf. Arist.de An.426a1

ψοφοδεής.definition: frightened at every noise, shy, timid, esp. of animals, Plu.Cam.27; Id.2.642a; of men, Pl.Phdr.257d, D.H.11.22, cf. PGrenf.2.7. 2 ; name of a play of Menander: timidity, Plu.Nic.2. Adv. Id.2.47b, Luc.Pr. Im.7, 28, Her…

ψοφοειδής.definition: noise-like, D.H.Comp.16. Adv. f.l. for Hsch

ψόφος.definition: noise (prop. of one thing striking against; mere sound, noise, your noise will never turn me, S.Aj.1116; E.Rh.565; Diog. ap.Arr.Epict.1.24.6; mere sounds, of high-sounding words or names, . . Men.737, cf. Alciphr.2.3,…

ψυγεῖον.definition: cooler, Hsch.; pl. prob. in IG22.1695.21

ψυδράκιον.definition: pimple, Dsc.5.109, cf. Damocr. ap.Gal.13.945; on the eyelid, stye, Cyran.35; on the nose, said to be caused by telling a lie, Sch.Theoc.12.24; cf. II

ψυκτήρ.definition: cool shady places for recreation, Nic.Thyat. ap. Ath.11.503c

ψυκτήριος.definition: cooling, i. e. fans, Achae.10, cf. Hp.Loc.Hom.27

ψύκτρα.definition: tray for drying figs on, Hsch. s.v

ψυχαγωγέω.definition: lead departed souls to the; evoke or conjure up the dead by sacrifice; hence metaph., lead or attract the souls of the living, win over, persuade, allure, Pl.Lg.909b; X.Mem.3.10.6; D.S.4.4; of speakers, Phld.Rh.1.148S…

ψυχαγωγία.definition: evocation of souls from the nether; metaph., winning of men's souls, persuasion, whence Rhetoric is called a by Pl.Phdr.261a, cf. 271c, Com.Adesp.199, Phld.Rh.1.148S.; also of poetry, Id.Po.2.61, al.:generally, gratif…

ψυχαγώγιον.definition: = a place where; air-hole, ventilator in the shafts of mines, Thphr.Ign.24

ψυχάζω.definition: refresh oneself in the shade, Alciphr.3.12, Ael.NA5.21, Procop.Gaz.p.175B

ψυχαῖος.definition: of the soul, Orac. Chald. ap. Lyd.Mens.1.11; Simp.in Ph.780.14

ψυχαπάτης.definition: beguiling the soul, Eratosth.36.5; AP5.165 ; AP12.256 , etc.; v

ψυχάριον.definition: Dim. of Pl.R.519a, Tht.195a, M.Ant.9.34, al., Jul.Or.7.206d, Herm.in Phdr.p.192A.; Epictet. ap. M.Ant.4.41

ψυχαστής.definition: one who cools himself in the shade: a play of Strattis

ψυχέμπορος.definition: trafficking in lives or men, Hsch

ψυχή.definition: life, Il.5.296, etc; metaph. of things dear as life, . . . Hes.Op.686; E.Andr.419; Timocl.35; so as an endearing name, Hld.1.8, al.; Juv.6.195; Mart.10.68

ψυχήϊος.definition: having a alive, living, Pythag. ap. Luc.Vit.Auct.6

ψυχίδιον.definition: Dim. of little soul, Luc.Nav.26, D.C.77.16

ψυχογονία.definition: the generation of the soul, Plu.2.415e, al., Herm.in Phdr.p.128A

ψυχοδαϊκτής.definition: destroying or killing the soul, epith. of Dionysus, AP9.524.24

ψυχοδοτήρ.definition: giver of the soul or life, epith. of Apollo, AP9.525.24

ψυχοειδής.definition: of the nature of soul, spiritual, Ph.1.15, 2.17, Theol.Ar.39

ψυχόλεθρος.definition: the death of the soul, Hdn.Epim.203

ψυχομαντεῖον.definition: place where the dead are conjured up, Plu.2.109c

ψυχομαχέω.definition: fight to the last gasp, fight; suffer anguish, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.4.21

ψυχοπλανής.definition: making the soul wander, epith. of Dionysus, AP9.524.24

ψυχοποιία.definition: the making of souls, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.68

ψυχοπομπεῖον.definition: a place where departed souls are conjured up, Plu.2.560e

ψυχοπομπός.definition: conductor or guide of souls, of; as Adj., Porph.Antr.8

ψυχοπότης.definition: drinking the life, i.e. the blood, Hsch. s.v

ψυχορραγέω.definition: let the soul break loose, i. e. lie at the last gasp, E.Alc.20, HF324, A.R.2.833, Plu.Crass.27, Hld.9.21

ψυχορραγής.definition: letting the soul break loose, hence lying at the last gasp, E.IT1466

ψυχορροφέω.definition: suck out the life, Phryn.PSp.128B; drink cold water, Pl.Com.259

ψυχοστασία.definition: weighing of lives: the title of a tragedy of A., in which Thetis and Eos weighed the lives of Achilles and Memnon against one another, and the latter was found lighter, Plu.2.17a

ψυχοτακής.definition: melting the soul or heart, AP5.55 ; APl.4.198

ψυχοταμίας.definition: keeper of souls, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69

ψυχουλκέομαι.definition: to be at the last gasp, LXX3 Ma.5.25

ψυχόω.definition: give soul to, APl.4.159; give a psychical character to physical sensations, Id.4.4.28

ψυχραίνω.definition: make cool or cold, cool, in Pass., Plu.Fr.inc.149, Alex.Trall.1.14, Procl.in Prm.p.571 S.: metaph., Id.Par.Ptol.270

ψυχρεύομαι.definition: furnish example of bad taste, Hermog.Id.1.6

ψυχρηλατέω.definition: hammer metal while it is cold, . . PMag.Par.1.2131

ψυχρήλατος.definition: cold-forged, of iron implements, Plu.2.434a, Asclep.Myrl. ap. Ath.11.501b, Ath.Mech.17.2, Plu.Brut.1: PMag.Par.1.1848

ψυχρία.definition: chilliness; metaph. of rhetoric, frigidity, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.50, cf. Plu.Alex.3

ψυχροβαφής.definition: dipped in cold water, Luc.Lex.5; imparted by a cold tincture, of colours and scents, Thphr.Od.22

ψυχροδοσία.definition: administration of cooling drinks, Herod.Med. ap. Aët.5.129

ψυχροδόχος.definition: receiving what is cold, cold- bath room, Luc.Hipp.7

ψυχροκοίλιος.definition: having a cold stomach, i. e. he diminishes the innate digestive heat, Ptol.Tetr.151

ψυχρολογέω.definition: talk nonsense, Luc.Pseudol.27; use silly arguments, Jul.Gal.347b

ψυχρολουσία.definition: a bathing in cold water, Hp.Mul.2.110, Thphr.Sud.16: pl., D.C.53.30, Sor.1.56

ψυχρολουτέω.definition: bathe in cold water, Ar.Fr.237, Hp.Morb.2.66, Plu.Alc.23, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.39.6, Agathin. ap. eund.10.7.6:—in codd. freq. written q. v

ψυχρολούτης.definition: bather in cold water, Lat. psychroluta Seneca Ep.53.3

ψυχρολουτρέω.definition: bathe in cold water, Arist.Pr.862b36, Str.3.3.6, Arr.Epict.1.1.29

ψυχρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be chilly, uninteresting, AP12.7

ψυχροποσία.definition: a drinking of cold water, Aret.SA2.6, Plu.2.692d, etc.: in pl., D.C.53.30

ψυχροποτέω.definition: drink cold water, Plu.2.60a, Antyll. ap. Orib.5.2.29

ψυχροπότης.definition: cold-water drinker, Plu.2.690b, cj. for in AP12.81

ψυχρότης.definition: coldness, cold, opp; metaph. of persons, want of feeling, bad taste, D.18.256: sluggishness, Plu.Fab.17

ψυχροφόρον.definition: = frigidarium, Gloss.: a water-pipe, PMag.Lond.121.397: lead tablet made out of a water-pipe, Tab.Defix.Aud.155 A28, B23

ψύχω.definition: Hdt.3.104, etc.: fut. Alex.25.10; make cool or cold , Hdt.3.104, cf. Hp.VM16 ; opp. Pl.Phdr.268b; Heraclit.126; Diph.56, cf. Isoc.15.287:—Pass., grow cool or cold, Hdt.4.181, Ar.Nu.151, Pl.Phd.71b, Arist.Pr.931a1; . .…

ψύχωσις.definition: a giving soul or life to, animating, quickening, Ph.1.15, Theol.Ar.48, M.Ant.12.24:—also, the principle of life, Philol. ap. Theol.Ar.55

ψυχωφελής.definition: profiting the soul or spirit, Suid.:—Subst. Id

ψωμίζω.definition: fut. Att. LXXNu.11.4:—feed by putting; give food by hand, Arist.HA592a30; bestow for food, 1 Ep.Cor.13.3

ψωμίον.definition: Dim. of of a bun for a crocodile, PTeb.33.14 , cf. D.L.6.37, Ev.Jo.13.26, M.Ant.7.3

ψώμισμα.definition: morsel, Democrat. ap. Arist.Rh.1407a7, Plu.Rom.2 , dub. l. in POxy.1088.39

ψωμόδουλος.definition: a slave to morsels of food, Hsch. s.v

ψωμοκόλαξ.definition: flatterer for morsels of bread, parasite, Ar.Fr.167 , Philem.8, Sannyr.10:—hence Philippid.8

ψωμοκόλαφος.definition: one who takes cuffs for the sake of morsels of bread, low parasite, Diph.49

ψωμόλεθρος.definition: bread-pest, Com. name for a parasite, Suid., Hdn.Epim.203:—also Zonar

ψώρα.definition: Ion. itch, mange, scurvy, of; metaph., Gal.8.148

ψωριάω.definition: to have the itch, scab, or mange, Hp.Aph.4.77; of trees, to be scabby, cankered, esp. of the fig, Thphr.CP5.9.10, HP4.14.3, etc.; of ib.8.10.1

ψωροφθαλμία.definition: a disease of the eyes, excessive dryness attended with itching, PMed.Strassb.p.6, Gal.14.766: pl., Dsc.1.68.5:— hence Gal.12.799; and a sufferer from blepharitis, Id.12.798

ψώχω.definition: rub small, Ev.Luc.6.1, cf. Dsc.5.159 :—Med., Nic.Th.629, cf

ψηλαφητικῶς.definition: Adv., by way of feeling, Eust.1717.16

ψιαθηδόν.definition: Adv. like rush-mats to expl. Sch.Th.2.75, Suid
